title: The Dream Weaver - Wikipedia
notes: Gary Wright, 1975: one of the first rock albums played mainly on electronic keyboards; Wright made the demos on keyboards and a drum machine. Drums: Andy Newmark and Jim Keltner.

title: Love Is Alive (Gary Wright song) - Wikipedia
notes: From The Dream Weaver (1975): Wright on vocals and keyboards, Andy Newmark on drums, all the music but the drums on keyboards. No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100; 27 weeks on the chart; No. 9 song of 1976.

title: More Than This (Roxy Music song) - Wikipedia
notes: The first single from Avalon (1982); personnel lists Andy Newmark on drums.

title: I've Got My Own Album to Do - Wikipedia
notes: Ronnie Wood's first solo album (1974): "the all-American rhythm section of Willie Weeks and Andy Newmark"; Newmark drums on tracks 1, 2 and 4-11, Micky Waller on 3. Keith Richards played the concerts in London with Wood to promote it.

title: Andy Newmark interview (Modern Drummer, 1984), as excerpted by Todd Bishop on Cruise Ship Drummer (6 July 2011; set-up excerpt 15 June 2024)
notes: In his words: "I stretch the time as far as I can. I put as much space as I can between every beat"; "I can sort of play behind the click a hair"; "I make believe in my mind that the machine is Ralph MacDonald, and he has a cowbell"; Kunkel, Gordon and Keltner's "real simple beats". The set-up excerpt (cruiseshipdrummer.com/2024/06/15/andy-newmarks-set-up/): a four-piece Yamaha (Recording and Tour series), 24" bass drum "for a big sound - I have a very, very heavy foot", 12" (or 13") rack tom, 16" floor tom, a 5 1/2 x 14 Yamaha snare; live tuned tight and "99% of the time ... a rimshot", in the studio "tune it way down and usually put a little piece of tape or a little Kleenex"; toms unmuffled, both heads alike; the bass drum flat with a blanket inside; Zildjian, a 20" K or A ride, two crashes of 16-18", 13" New Beat hats, "the smallest that Zildjian makes"; "Ninety-five percent of the time, I'm playing only hihat, snare and bass drum."

title: E29: Live From My Drum Room With Andy Newmark! 3-28-21 (YouTube, cUQftJ6IFVs)
notes: Read from the video's captions (two hours). Fresh was played to "a really old-fashioned little rhythm ... a rumba, a cha-cha, a tango, rock one and rock two"; "I played along with the Rhythm Ace on the Fresh album and Gary's album. If you heard just the drums on Fresh and the Rhythm Ace, I'm all over the place ... I am not locked in with the machine. I'll move ahead. Then you hear it in the cans. I compensate"; Love Is Alive "done to a Rhythm Ace ... just like Fresh"; "The way I played on Fresh and Love Is Alive ... That's the way I always played"; Anticipation, the brushes and "big open fills like Ringo and Russ Kunkel", was the departure. Avalon: Bryan Ferry made the basic tracks alone with a drum machine; Newmark and Neil Jason played to it live at the Power Station; "most of it's played in real time", fills included. Watching Jim Gordon record You're So Vain taught him "conviction and owning every note"; "It was only when I saw Tony Williams when I was about 19 that my mind expanded"; Rick Marotta, his roommate, sent him to Carly Simon's audition and "set me straight when I started overplaying". First lesson at nine (1959), Haskell Harr's drum book; Yamaha since the 1982 Roxy Music tour in Japan.

title: In Time - Sly & the Family Stone - DRUM TRANSCRIPTION (Massimo Malaguti, YouTube, vn_OaiqLllU)
notes: A score of 17 bars of 4/4, shown on screen and played over the record: its audio lines up with the record at 40.5 s, the start of verse 1. The hat in sixteenths, opened on the "a" of 1 and closed by the foot on 2; the snare on the "e" of 1, the "and" of 3 and the "e" of 4, accented, none on 2 or 4; the kick on 1, the "e" of 3 and the "a" of 4; variations in every bar.

title: Groove o' the day: Let Me Have It All - Andy Newmark (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 10 December 2025)
notes: Ten bars at 94 from 0:28, with a PDF (pdxdrummer.com). "Busy, with a lot of variety, based on a loose idea of a two measure groove ... He fills through the 1 at a number of points"; "there may be some studio tomfoolery happening, like a second drum track hiding in the mix".

title: Groove o' the day: Andy Newmark - Babies Makin' Babies (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 28 December 2018)
notes: The main groove and five variations of the alternate version (2007 reissue), all in its first minute: "a cool 70s funk groove in a James Brown mode ... The hihat is played one-handed". Sixteenths on the hat, the snare on the "and" of 1 and on 4. Not scored here.

notes: Carly Simon (1971): "every single measure is different"; much of the riding on a crash, the hat foot in eighths. Not scored here.
